why_this_file_exists.summary: write-provenance.mjs only records a sha_after when it can match a preceding --before for the same path. Any further edit to a file AFTER its --before/--after pair has been stamped is invisible to the record: re-running --after prints 'no matching --before record; ignoring' and changes nothing.
why_this_file_exists.why_not_fixed_in_place: The only way to make the helper stamp a fresh sha_after is to run --before again first. That would overwrite sha_before with the CURRENT (post-refactor) content, falsely recording the post-run state as the pre-run state and breaking /mmo:revert for those files. Leaving sha_before correct and sha_after stale is the safe failure direction, so that is what was done.
why_this_file_exists.revert_impact: LOW and fail-safe. /mmo:revert restores from sha_before / backup_path / git, all of which are correct. sha_after feeds only the 'has a later run touched this file?' dirty-check, so a stale value makes revert MORE cautious, not less.
why_this_file_exists.relationship_to_other_defects: This is very likely the same root cause as CMP-103's recorded PROV-1 ('provenance backup is a mid-run intermediate'). Both are the helper mishandling multi-round edits to one path. Worth filing together.

duplicate_entry_hazard.summary: Five paths have TWO entries in files_touched. For the four shim files this is actively dangerous: the SECOND entry's backup contains a MID-RUN INTERMEDIATE, not the pre-run state.
duplicate_entry_hazard.how_it_happened: Stage S1 rewrote the four per-view files into thin shims. Provenance recorded entry #1 with the correct pre-run sha_before and backup=no (the files were clean and tracked, so git holds the original). At Gate 3 the user directed deleting the shims. write-provenance --before ran again; this time the files were DIRTY, so the helper took a backup - of the SHIM content it had itself helped create - and recorded that as sha_before on entry #2.
duplicate_entry_hazard.revert_rule: For these four paths the AUTHORITATIVE pre-run state is ENTRY #1 (sha_before against git HEAD 2d81253a). ENTRY #2's backup_path must be IGNORED - restoring it would resurrect the shim, which never existed before this run and which the run deliberately deleted. Correct revert is: restore from git HEAD.
duplicate_entry_hazard.fifth_path_is_benign: packages/web/src/views/Week/interaction/adapter/commit-characterization.test.ts also has 2 entries, but it is a NEW file in both, so existed_before is false on entry #1 and revert correctly deletes it.
duplicate_entry_hazard.confirms_hypothesis: This is the third distinct manifestation of the same root cause in one run, and it is almost certainly what CMP-103 recorded as PROV-1 ('provenance backup for EventJoinIcon.tsx is a mid-run intermediate; on revert that file must be DELETED, never restored'). write-provenance.mjs has no concept of a path it has already seen: every --before overwrites the run's belief about the pre-run state with whatever is on disk at that moment.
duplicate_entry_hazard.suggested_fix: write-provenance.mjs --before should be idempotent per path per run: if an entry for that path already exists, do not overwrite sha_before/backup_path, only append to a rounds[] list.

audit_at_reconciliation.note: The 2 null/deleted entries are the two targeting test files removed in stage S2; their sha_before and tracked_in_git are correct, which is what revert needs.
